You are implementing fixes in the Rust backend of a Tauri v2 macOS app at /Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src-tauri. First read /Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/IMPROVEMENTS.md sections "A. Desktop app — Rust backend" and "Top priorities" for context (findings A2, A6, A17-A21, C3). You own ONLY Rust files under src-tauri/src/ (do NOT touch tauri.conf.json — another agent owns it, and do NOT touch any TypeScript). Do not commit.

Implement exactly these fixes:

1. **Recording state latch (audio.rs:87 area)**: every error path after `state.is_recording.store(true, ...)` in `start_recording_with_device` must reset `is_recording` (and any partially-set state like app_handle) before returning. Use a drop-guard struct or restructure so the flag is only set after `stream.play()` succeeds. Verify all error returns (no-device, config, WavWriter::create, unsupported format, play).

2. **Mic-missing fallback (audio.rs:99-102 area)**: when a device name is given but no matching device exists, fall back to the default input device instead of erroring (log a warning). Only error if there's no input device at all.

3. **Stream error surfacing (audio.rs:121-124)**: the cpal `err_fn` currently only does `eprintln!`. Capture the AppHandle and emit event `recording-error` with payload `{ "message": string }`, and make sure recording state is cleaned up (clear is_recording so the next hotkey press works). The frontend is being updated in parallel to listen for exactly this event name/payload.

4. **WAV retention (new)**: after every successful transcription (both the whisper path in handlers/whisper.rs and the parakeet path in handlers/parakeet.rs), prune the recordings directory (see `get_save_path` in audio.rs:243-258) to keep only the 20 newest .wav files by modification time, deleting the rest. Put the helper in audio.rs (e.g. `cleanup_old_recordings(app_handle, keep: usize)`), tolerate IO errors with a log rather than failing the transcription.

5. **Model download hardening (handlers/models.rs)** — this is the big one:
   - **In-flight guard**: track in-flight downloads (e.g. a `Mutex<HashSet<String>>` in managed state or a static); a second `download_model` call for a model already downloading returns Err("download already in progress"). Always remove from the set on completion/failure (drop guard).
   - **Resume**: do NOT delete the existing `.download.tmp` before starting (currently at ~line 183-189). If it exists, send a `Range: bytes=<len>-` header; on HTTP 206 open the file in append mode; on 200 truncate and restart. Keep the atomic rename to the final destination on completion.
   - **Cancellation**: add a new command `cancel_model_download(model_id: String) -> Result<(), String>` (register it in lib.rs). Use a cancellation flag (e.g. per-model `Arc<AtomicBool>` stored alongside the in-flight set) checked in the download loop; on cancel, stop cleanly and KEEP the .tmp file so a later download resumes. Emit a final event or just return — frontend handles UI.
   - **Timeouts**: replace the 1-hour total request timeout with a connect timeout (~30s) plus a per-chunk/stall timeout (e.g. wrap chunk reads in `tokio::time::timeout` of ~60s), so slow-but-alive connections aren't killed.
   - **Async IO**: replace blocking `std::fs::File::create`/`write_all` in the download loop with `tokio::fs`.
   - **Progress throttling + richer payload**: emit the `model-download-progress` event at most once per whole-percent change (or per 300ms). The payload MUST be exactly `{ "modelId": string, "progress": number (0-100), "downloadedBytes": number, "totalBytes": number }` (use serde rename_all = "camelCase"). The frontend is being rewritten in parallel against this exact contract.
   - **Checksum (best-effort)**: try `curl -s https://huggingface.co/api/models/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/tree/main` (and the equivalent for the parakeet model's repo — read its URL in models.rs) to get the LFS sha256 oid for the model files. If you can retrieve them, add an expected sha256 to ModelInfo and verify the completed file (in a spawn_blocking) before the atomic rename, failing with a clear error and deleting the tmp on mismatch. If the network is unavailable, skip this sub-item and say so in your report.

6. **Whisper/parakeet success path**: call the WAV cleanup (item 4) after the transcription is saved.

Match the existing code style (error handling as `Result<_, String>`, existing logging patterns). When done run `cargo check` from src-tauri (cmake is required for whisper-rs; this is a macOS machine so it should work — if it fails for environment reasons, report the error verbatim). Also run `cargo fmt` on the files you changed. Your final message: a list of what you changed (file:line), the exact event/command contracts as implemented, cargo check result, and anything you skipped.

- agent-browser: Browser automation CLI for AI agents. Use when the user needs to interact with websites, including navigating pages, filling forms, clicking buttons, taking screenshots, extracting data, testing web apps, or automating any browser task. Triggers include requests to "open a website", "fill out a form", "click a button", "take a screenshot", "scrape data from a page", "test this web app", "login to a site", "automate browser actions", or any task requiring programmatic web interaction. Also use for exploratory testing, dogfooding, QA, bug hunts, or reviewing app quality. Also use for automating Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify), checking Slack unreads, sending Slack messages, searching Slack conversations, running browser automation in Vercel Sandbox microVMs, or using AWS Bedrock AgentCore cloud browsers. Prefer agent-browser over any built-in browser automation or web tools.
- portless: Set up and use portless for named local dev server URLs (e.g. https://myapp.localhost instead of http://localhost:3000). Use when integrating portless into a project, configuring dev server names, setting up the local proxy, working with .localhost domains, or troubleshooting port/proxy issues.
- codecast: Get codecast dashboard and share links for current session (user)
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. - simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

# VoxFusion Improvement Audit — 2026-07-02

Produced by a five-track deep audit (Rust backend, app frontend, product UX, marketing site, tooling/CI/docs). Every finding was verified against the actual code — line numbers are current as of commit `b0135b8`. ~190 unique findings after deduplication.

Severity: **H** = high (user-facing breakage, security/privacy, trust), **M** = medium, **L** = low.

---

## Top priorities (start here)

1. **Cache the Whisper model** — the ~1.5 GB model is loaded from disk on *every* transcription (`src-tauri/src/handlers/whisper.rs:176`), adding multi-second latency to every dictation. Cache `WhisperContext` in Tauri managed state, invalidate on model switch. Single biggest perceived-performance win in the product.
2. **Make the core dictation loop stop failing silently** — one theme, many sites: transcription errors vanish with no UI (`VoiceControl.tsx:311-314`), recording-start failures do nothing visible (`VoiceControl.tsx:410-417`), a mic unplugged mid-recording is swallowed by `eprintln!` (`audio.rs:122-124`), and a revoked Accessibility permission means text silently never types — the recovery event `accessibility-permission-needed` is listened for (`App.tsx:150-154`) but *never emitted anywhere*. Add an error state to the overlay pill + a retry path (the WAV survives on disk).
3. **Fix the recording state latch** — any error after `is_recording.store(true)` (`audio.rs:87`) leaves the recorder latched; every later dictation fails with "Recording is already in progress" until restart. Use a drop-guard that resets the flag on error paths.
4. **The overlay window ignores the user's default style** — `initSettings()` only runs in the main window; the voice-control window is a separate JS context, so `settings().defaultStyle` is always `"default"` (`VoiceControl.tsx:100,309`). User-facing data bug on every transcription.
5. **Close the security holes as a set** — `"csp": null` (`tauri.conf.json:44`) + every system-wide keystroke broadcast into the webview (`system_key_watcher.rs:133-146`) + `read_audio_file` accepting arbitrary absolute paths (`handlers/text.rs:12`) compose into: any webview compromise = system keylogger + arbitrary file exfiltration. Set a CSP, match hotkeys in Rust, and restrict paths to the recordings dir.
6. **Tell one honest privacy story** — the product's positioning ("local-first, 0 data sent to servers") is contradicted by: PostHog running unconditionally with no consent or opt-out (`src/lib/posthog.ts:25-39`), every dictation WAV kept on disk forever with no cleanup (`audio.rs:244-258`), the marketing hero stat "0 data sent to servers", a privacy policy that never names PostHog/Umami, and a README claiming "no servers". Fix together: analytics opt-out toggle + onboarding disclosure, WAV deletion after transcription (or retention setting), reworded marketing claims ("0 *audio* sent to servers"), updated policy.
7. **Harden the 1.5 GB model download** — not resumable (partial deleted before every retry, `models.rs:183-189`), not cancellable, no checksum (URL pins mutable `resolve/main`), no in-flight guard (double-click = two writers on the same temp file), 1-hour *total* timeout kills slow connections, and progress events fire per chunk (hundreds of thousands of IPC events). Add Range resume, cancel, SHA-256 + pinned revision, per-model in-flight lock, and emit on whole-percent change.
8. **`panic = "abort"` defeats every `catch_unwind`** (`Cargo.toml:62` vs `apps.rs:238,270,347`) — a malformed `Info.plist`/`.icns` in /Applications, or an ObjC exception in `get_frontmost_app` (runs at the start of *every* dictation), aborts the whole app in release. Drop `panic = "abort"` or stop relying on catch_unwind.
9. **Hotkeys permanently die if Accessibility isn't granted at first watcher start** — `addGlobalMonitorForEventsMatchingMask_handler` returns `None`, it's silently forgotten, and the `WATCHER_RUNNING` latch blocks all retries until app restart (`system_key_watcher.rs:160,176-193`).
10. **Onboarding dead-end: denied microphone permission** — no "Open System Settings" link and no skip; once macOS TCC denies, every retry auto-fails and the user is stuck on step 1 forever (`MicrophonePermissionStep.tsx:35-51`).
11. **Marketing says the wrong hotkey** — site teaches `Cmd+;` in three places (`i18n/ru/hero.ts:6`, `features.ts:8`, `index.astro:83`); the app default is `LeftControl+LeftOption` (`hotkeyUtils.ts:44`). Also: Terms prohibit decompiling / competing products for an MIT-licensed app with a public repo — direct license contradiction.
12. **No CI whatsoever** — no PR checks, and `release.yml` ships from a tag with zero lint/typecheck/test gates. Add a `ci.yml` (biome, tsc, astro check, vite build on ubuntu; `cargo check`/`cargo test` on macos) and make release depend on it.
13. **Update progress bar is mathematically broken** — raw chunk *bytes* accumulate into the percent signal and render as `width: bytes/10 %`, pegging at 100% after ~1 KB (`UpdateNotification.tsx:103-105,152`); `contentLength` is checked but never stored. Also no changelog shown, no dismiss button.

### Quick wins (minutes each, big payoff)

- **One-file tsconfig fix kills all ~1157 `astro check` errors**: marketingsite tsconfig inherits the root's repo-wide `include` + `jsx: "react-jsx"`, so it type-checks the app's Solid TSX as React. Change to `"extends": "astro/tsconfigs/strict"`, `"include": ["src", ".astro/types.d.ts"]`.
- **Two-line biome.json override makes `bun run lint` exit clean**: add `noUnusedImports: off` + `useImportType: off` to the `**/*.astro` override.
- **Docs' first command is broken**: `bun run tauri:dev` doesn't exist (README:50, CONTRIBUTING:33, AGENTS:20) — the script is `dev`.
- **Home-screen hotkey hint is hardcoded to the default hotkey** (`en.ts:219,292-293`) — users with a custom hotkey are shown wrong instructions on the main screen. Interpolate `hotkeyDisplayName(settings().hotkey)` as `LearningStep.tsx:36` already does.
- **`bun install --frozen-lockfile`** in release.yml:40 and the Dockerfile.
- **Remove the squatting-risk updater endpoint** — `tauri.conf.json:50-53` tries `github.com/voxfusion/voxfusion` first, an org that doesn't match the actual repo owner.

---

## A. Desktop app — Rust backend (src-tauri)

### High
- **A1 (H)** `Cargo.toml:62` + `apps.rs:238,270,347` — `panic = "abort"` makes `catch_unwind` useless; malformed plist/icns or ObjC exception aborts the app (see Top #8).
- **A2 (H)** `audio.rs:87` — errors after `is_recording.store(true)` latch the recorder forever (see Top #3).

## Top priorities (start here)

1. **Cache the Whisper model** — the ~1.5 GB model is loaded from disk on *every* transcription (`src-tauri/src/handlers/whisper.rs:176`), adding multi-second latency to every dictation. Cache `WhisperContext` in Tauri managed state, invalidate on model switch. Single biggest perceived-performance win in the product.
2. **Make the core dictation loop stop failing silently** — one theme, many sites: transcription errors vanish with no UI (`VoiceControl.tsx:311-314`), recording-start failures do nothing visible (`VoiceControl.tsx:410-417`), a mic unplugged mid-recording is swallowed by `eprintln!` (`audio.rs:122-124`), and a revoked Accessibility permission means text silently never types — the recovery event `accessibility-permission-needed` is listened for (`App.tsx:150-154`) but *never emitted anywhere*. Add an error state to the overlay pill + a retry path (the WAV survives on disk).
3. **Fix the recording state latch** — any error after `is_recording.store(true)` (`audio.rs:87`) leaves the recorder latched; every later dictation fails with "Recording is already in progress" until restart. Use a drop-guard that resets the flag on error paths.
4. **The overlay window ignores the user's default style** — `initSettings()` only runs in the main window; the voice-control window is a separate JS context, so `settings().defaultStyle` is always `"default"` (`VoiceControl.tsx:100,309`). User-facing data bug on every transcription.
5. **Close the security holes as a set** — `"csp": null` (`tauri.conf.json:44`) + every system-wide keystroke broadcast into the webview (`system_key_watcher.rs:133-146`) + `read_audio_file` accepting arbitrary absolute paths (`handlers/text.rs:12`) compose into: any webview compromise = system keylogger + arbitrary file exfiltration. Set a CSP, match hotkeys in Rust, and restrict paths to the recordings dir.
6. **Tell one honest privacy story** — the product's positioning ("local-first, 0 data sent to servers") is contradicted by: PostHog running unconditionally with no consent or opt-out (`src/lib/posthog.ts:25-39`), every dictation WAV kept on disk forever with no cleanup (`audio.rs:244-258`), the marketing hero stat "0 data sent to servers", a privacy policy that never names PostHog/Umami, and a README claiming "no servers". Fix together: analytics opt-out toggle + onboarding disclosure, WAV deletion after transcription (or retention setting), reworded marketing claims ("0 *audio* sent to servers"), updated policy.
7. **Harden the 1.5 GB model download** — not resumable (partial deleted before every retry, `models.rs:183-189`), not cancellable, no checksum (URL pins mutable `resolve/main`), no in-flight guard (double-click = two writers on the same temp file), 1-hour *total* timeout kills slow connections, and progress events fire per chunk (hundreds of thousands of IPC events). Add Range resume, cancel, SHA-256 + pinned revision, per-model in-flight lock, and emit on whole-percent change.
8. **`panic = "abort"` defeats every `catch_unwind`** (`Cargo.toml:62` vs `apps.rs:238,270,347`) — a malformed `Info.plist`/`.icns` in /Applications, or an ObjC exception in `get_frontmost_app` (runs at the start of *every* dictation), aborts the whole app in release. Drop `panic = "abort"` or stop relying on catch_unwind.
9. **Hotkeys permanently die if Accessibility isn't granted at first watcher start** — `addGlobalMonitorForEventsMatchingMask_handler` returns `None`, it's silently forgotten, and the `WATCHER_RUNNING` latch blocks all retries until app restart (`system_key_watcher.rs:160,176-193`).
10. **Onboarding dead-end: denied microphone permission** — no "Open System Settings" link and no skip; once macOS TCC denies, every retry auto-fails and the user is stuck on step 1 forever (`MicrophonePermissionStep.tsx:35-51`).
11. **Marketing says the wrong hotkey** — site teaches `Cmd+;` in three places (`i18n/ru/hero.ts:6`, `features.ts:8`, `index.astro:83`); the app default is `LeftControl+LeftOption` (`hotkeyUtils.ts:44`). Also: Terms prohibit decompiling / competing products for an MIT-licensed app with a public repo — direct license contradiction.
12. **No CI whatsoever** — no PR checks, and `release.yml` ships from a tag with zero lint/typecheck/test gates. Add a `ci.yml` (biome, tsc, astro check, vite build on ubuntu; `cargo check`/`cargo test` on macos) and make release depend on it.
13. **Update progress bar is mathematically broken** — raw chunk *bytes* accumulate into the percent signal and render as `width: bytes/10 %`, pegging at 100% after ~1 KB (`UpdateNotification.tsx:103-105,152`); `contentLength` is checked but never stored. Also no changelog shown, no dismiss button.

### Quick wins (minutes each, big payoff)

- **One-file tsconfig fix kills all ~1157 `astro check` errors**: marketingsite tsconfig inherits the root's repo-wide `include` + `jsx: "react-jsx"`, so it type-checks the app's Solid TSX as React. Change to `"extends": "astro/tsconfigs/strict"`, `"include": ["src", ".astro/types.d.ts"]`.
- **Two-line biome.json override makes `bun run lint` exit clean**: add `noUnusedImports: off` + `useImportType: off` to the `**/*.astro` override.
- **Docs' first command is broken**: `bun run tauri:dev` doesn't exist (README:50, CONTRIBUTING:33, AGENTS:20) — the script is `dev`.
- **Home-screen hotkey hint is hardcoded to the default hotkey** (`en.ts:219,292-293`) — users with a custom hotkey are shown wrong instructions on the main screen. Interpolate `hotkeyDisplayName(settings().hotkey)` as `LearningStep.tsx:36` already does.
- **`bun install --frozen-lockfile`** in release.yml:40 and the Dockerfile.
- **Remove the squatting-risk updater endpoint** — `tauri.conf.json:50-53` tries `github.com/voxfusion/voxfusion` first, an org that doesn't match the actual repo owner.

---

## A. Desktop app — Rust backend (src-tauri)

### High
- **A1 (H)** `Cargo.toml:62` + `apps.rs:238,270,347` — `panic = "abort"` makes `catch_unwind` useless; malformed plist/icns or ObjC exception aborts the app (see Top #8).
- **A2 (H)** `audio.rs:87` — errors after `is_recording.store(true)` latch the recorder forever (see Top #3).

All done. Final report:

## Changes implemented

**1. Recording state latch** — `src/handlers/audio.rs`
- `start_recording_with_device` no longer sets `is_recording` up front. All state (`app_handle`, `save_path`, `writer`, `stream`) is stored only after `stream.play()` succeeds, and `is_recording.store(true)` is the very last step (audio.rs:218-225). Every error return (no device, config, `WavWriter::create`, unsupported format, build/play failure) now leaves the recorder unlatched. Concurrency is still safe: the whole function runs under the `RECORDING_STATE` mutex.

**2. Mic-missing fallback** — audio.rs:101-121
- A named device that no longer exists falls back to the default input device with `log::warn!(target: "audio", "input device not found, falling back to default device_name=...")`. It only errors if there is no input device at all.

**3. Stream error surfacing** — audio.rs:136-150
- `err_fn` now captures the `AppHandle` and the `is_recording` Arc; on a cpal stream error it logs via `log::error!`, clears `is_recording` (so the next hotkey press works), and emits `recording-error`.

**4. WAV retention** — audio.rs:275-282 (`recordings_dir`), audio.rs:293-337 (`cleanup_old_recordings(app_handle, keep)`), `RECORDINGS_TO_KEEP = 20` (audio.rs:59). Keeps the 20 newest `.wav` files by mtime; all IO errors log-and-continue, never failing the transcription.

**5. Model download hardening** — `src/handlers/models.rs`
- In-flight guard: `ACTIVE_DOWNLOADS: LazyLock<Mutex<HashMap<String, Arc<AtomicBool>>>>` (models.rs:177) + `DownloadGuard` drop-guard (models.rs:182-192); duplicate call returns `Err("download already in progress")` (models.rs:200). Guard lives inside `download_model_file`, so `download_whisper_model` is covered too.
- Resume: leftover `.download.tmp` is no longer deleted; sends `Range: bytes=<len>-`; HTTP 206 → append mode, 200 → truncate/restart (models.rs:336-368). An oversized tmp is discarded; a byte-complete tmp skips the network and goes straight to validation (models.rs:273-286). Short/incomplete downloads now *keep* the tmp for the next resume. Atomic rename retained (models.rs:309).
- Cancellation: `cancel_model_download` command (models.rs:555) sets the per-model `AtomicBool`; the loop polls it every 250 ms, flushes, keeps the tmp, and returns `Err("Download cancelled")` (models.rs:379-384).
- Timeouts: `connect_timeout(30s)` replaces the 1-hour total timeout; a 60 s per-chunk stall timeout is implemented via 250 ms `tokio::time::timeout` slices (models.rs:166-173, 374-398).
- Async IO: download loop uses `tokio::fs::File`/`OpenOptions` + `AsyncWriteExt::write_all`/`flush`.
- Progress throttling: emitted at most once per whole-percent change (or per 300 ms when total unknown) (models.rs:410-421).
- Checksum: `ModelInfo.sha256` added (models.rs:43) and populated from the HF LFS API (network was available): whisper `1fc70f774d38eb169993ac391eea357ef47c88757ef72ee5943879b7e8e2bc69`, parakeet `e8bc983c89342a1f36a5bfa1a7a2dc6fab8f9ebdc2e305738f36e3ff60cbc313` — both sizes match the existing `expected_size`. Verification runs in `spawn_blocking` before the rename; mismatch deletes the tmp and returns a clear error (models.rs:434-460).
- Registration: `cancel_model_download` re-exported in `src/handlers/mod.rs:28` and registered in `src/lib.rs:10,82`. Added `sha2 = "0.10"` to `Cargo.toml:39`.

**6. Success-path cleanup** — whisper path calls `cleanup_old_recordings` at whisper.rs:302; parakeet path at parakeet.rs:116 (covers the early-return branch in `transcribe_audio`).

## Exact contracts (frontend-facing)
- Event `recording-error`, payload `{ "message": string }`.
- Event `model-download-progress`, payload `{ "modelId": string, "progress": number 0-100, "downloadedBytes": number, "totalBytes": number }` (serde camelCase; `totalBytes` is 0 only if length is unknown and no expected size exists — never for the two registry models).
- Command `cancel_model_download(modelId: string) -> Result<(), String>`; errors with `"No download in progress for <id>"` if nothing is in flight. The in-flight `download_model` call then rejects with `"Download cancelled"`.
- Duplicate `download_model` rejects with `"download already in progress"`.

## Verification
- `cargo check` from src-tauri: **Finished, zero warnings, zero errors** (run twice, after edits and after `rustfmt`).
- `rustfmt --edition 2024` run on all six changed files.
- Nothing skipped — checksum retrieval succeeded for both repos.

Note: the working tree also contains diffs in `apps.rs`, `media.rs`, `sites.rs`, `tauri.conf.json`, and marketing-site files from other parallel agents — those are not mine and were left untouched. Nothing committed, per instructions.
